_disclosure: SYNTHETIC. Illustrative patient profile authored for this project. Not derived from any real patient, any real record, or the source video's actual (unknown) patient. Values were chosen to represent a technically demanding but entirely plausible RARP candidate, so the elevated-prior markers and the risk summary have something real to show. Every surface that renders these fields must label them synthetic.

_provenance.basis: Field set and value ranges chosen to be clinically plausible for a RARP candidate. Not sampled from any dataset.

anesthetic_risk.asa_note: Severe systemic disease — hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity.

surgical_plan.nerve_sparing_note: Bilateral partial nerve-sparing intended; right side may be sacrificed if intraoperative findings suggest extracapsular extension.

risk_flags.relevance: Longer operative time, harder pelvic exposure, higher airway pressures under steep Trendelenburg.
Impaired wound healing and higher infection risk.
Scarred bladder neck with obliterated tissue planes.
Raises the cost of thermal or traction injury near the neurovascular bundle.

elevated_priors.reason: Obesity increases operative time, complicates pelvic exposure, and raises airway pressures under steep Trendelenburg.
ASA 3 indicates severe systemic disease and a higher perioperative risk profile.
Prostate volume above ~40 mL is associated with more difficult bladder-neck dissection.
A median lobe distorts the bladder neck and complicates its dissection and reconstruction.
Shorter membranous urethra is associated with slower return of continence.
Prior TURP scars the bladder neck and obliterates normal tissue planes.
